title: EG4 · Energy
description: EG4 12000XP daily, monthly and lifetime energy (solar, consumption, battery) from the EG4 cloud.

links.title: Energy
links.tooltip: EG4 · Energy — daily, monthly and lifetime energy

panels.title: Solar today
panels.description: Solar energy produced today, both MPPTs combined (pv1_energy_today; the cloud has no per-string energy). Latest reading of the inverter's daily counter, which resets at local midnight (America/Los_Angeles). EG4 cloud data: a new sample only arrives when EG4 publishes (about every 1-2 min, sometimes 5).

targets.query:
from(bucket: "luxmon")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "luxmon_register" and r._field == "value" and r.name == "pv1_energy_today")
  |> last()
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["_time"])
  |> last()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({_time: r._time, "Solar": r._value}))

panels.title: Self-sufficiency today
panels.description: Share of today's consumption not supplied by grid or generator: 1 − grid_import_today ÷ load_energy_today (grid import is always 0 on this off-grid site). The EG4 cloud has no generator-energy counter, so generator energy cannot be subtracted: see 'Generator today' next to it. If the generator ran, this percentage is overstated. Blank while today's consumption is still 0. EG4 cloud data: a new sample only arrives when EG4 publishes (about every 1-2 min, sometimes 5).

targets.query:
import "internal/debug"

from(bucket: "luxmon")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "luxmon_register" and r._field == "value" and (r.name == "load_energy_today" or r.name == "grid_import_today"))
  |> last()
  |> group(columns: ["name"])
  |> sort(columns: ["_time"])
  |> last()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({k: 1, name: r.name, _value: r._value}))
  |> group()
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["k"], columnKey: ["name"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => exists r.load_energy_today)
  |> map(fn: (r) => {
      grid = if exists r.grid_import_today then r.grid_import_today else 0.0
      return {"Self-sufficiency": if r.load_energy_today > 0.0 then 100.0 * (1.0 - grid / r.load_energy_today) else debug.null(type: "float")}
    })

panels.title: Generator today
panels.description: Whether the generator input showed voltage or frequency above 20 (gen_voltage, gen_frequency) at any sample today. There is no generator-energy counter, so generator energy is not counted in self-sufficiency; if it ran, self-sufficiency is overstated. Samples arrive every 1–2 min (sometimes 5) from the EG4 cloud, so a very short run can be missed.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "luxmon")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "luxmon_register" and r._field == "value" and (r.name == "gen_voltage" or r.name == "gen_frequency"))
  |> group()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({_time: r._time, _value: if r._value > 20.0 then 1 else 0}))
  |> max()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({"Generator": r._value}))

panels.title: Solar ÷ consumption today
panels.description: Solar today ÷ consumption today (pv1_energy_today ÷ load_energy_today). Over 100% means solar exceeded what the house used; the surplus charged the battery or was curtailed. Low early in the day is normal. EG4 cloud data: a new sample only arrives when EG4 publishes (about every 1-2 min, sometimes 5).

from(bucket: "luxmon")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)

panels.title: Data freshness
panels.description: Age of the newest EG4 sample. Fresh under 6 min, Delayed 6–10 min, Stale over 10 min. Data comes from the EG4 cloud, so 1–2 min (sometimes 5) between samples is normal.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "luxmon")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "luxmon_register" and r._field == "value" and r.name == "soc")
  |> last()
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["_time"])
  |> last()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({
      _time: r._time,
      "Status": float(v: int(v: now()) - int(v: r._time)) / 1000000000.0,
      "Last update": int(v: r._time) / 1000000,
    }))

panels.title: Daily energy
panels.description: Solar vs consumption per local day (America/Los_Angeles): the day's highest reading of the daily counters pv1_energy_today (both MPPTs combined) and load_energy_today. The counters run from midnight, so a day is complete even if sampling started late. If a counter resets a little after midnight (inverter clock behind), the readings before the reset still hold yesterday's total and are ignored. Today is marked '(so far)'. Days with no samples are left out, not drawn as zero; history starts 8 May 2026 (install day; imported from the EG4 portal export). EG4 cloud data: a new sample only arrives when EG4 publishes (about every 1-2 min, sometimes 5).

panels.title: Daily battery in / out
panels.description: Battery energy in vs out per local day (America/Los_Angeles): the day's highest reading of charge_energy_today and discharge_energy_today, ignoring pre-reset readings just after midnight. Today is marked '(so far)'. Days with no samples are left out, not drawn as zero; history starts 8 May 2026 (install day; imported from the EG4 portal export). EG4 cloud data: a new sample only arrives when EG4 publishes (about every 1-2 min, sometimes 5).

panels.title: Monthly energy · last 12 months
panels.description: Solar vs consumption per local calendar month: the change in the lifetime counters (pv1_energy_total, load_energy_total) from the previous month's month-end reading to this month's. The very first month with data starts from the counter at local midnight of its first sampled day and says so, e.g. 'May 2026 (from 8th)'; the current month is marked '(so far)'. Months with no samples are left out (a fully missing month's energy lands in the next month with data). Always the 12 previous months plus this month, whatever the dashboard time range. EG4 cloud data: a new sample only arrives when EG4 publishes (about every 1-2 min, sometimes 5).

targets.query:
import "timezone"
import "date"

loc = timezone.location(name: "America/Los_Angeles")
months = ["Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun", "Jul", "Aug", "Sep", "Oct", "Nov", "Dec"]
thisMonth = date.truncate(t: now(), unit: 1mo, location: loc)
shownFrom = date.truncate(t: v.timeRangeStart, unit: 1mo, location: loc)

// One extra day before the range, so the first shown month is measured from the previous
// month's last counter reading. Only the very first month with data needs a baseline.
src = from(bucket: "luxmon")
  |> range(start: date.sub(d: 1d, from: v.timeRangeStart), stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "luxmon_register" and r._field == "value" and (r.name == "pv1_energy_total" or r.name == "load_energy_total" or r.name == "pv1_energy_today" or r.name == "load_energy_today"))

// Lifetime counter at the end of each local calendar month (its highest = last reading).
monthEnd = src
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.name == "pv1_energy_total" or r.name == "load_energy_total")
  |> group(columns: ["name"])
  |> aggregateWindow(every: 1mo, fn: max, createEmpty: false, timeSrc: "_start", location: loc)
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({_time: date.truncate(t: r._time, unit: 1mo, location: loc), _value: r._value, series: if r.name == "pv1_energy_total" then "Solar" else "Consumption"}))
  |> group(columns: ["series"])

// Baseline for the first month with data: the lifetime counter at local midnight of the first
// sampled day (lifetime total minus that day's counter, from the first sample carrying both).
firstRow = src
  |> limit(n: 60)
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({_time: r._time, _value: r._value, series: if r.name =~ /^pv1_/ then "Solar" else "Consumption", kind: if r.name =~ /_total$/ then "total" else "today"}))
  |> group(columns: ["series"])
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["_time"], columnKey: ["kind"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => exists r.total and exists r.today)
  |> sort(columns: ["_time"])
  |> first(column: "total")
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({
      series: r.series,
      _time: date.sub(d: 1mo, from: date.truncate(t: r._time, unit: 1mo, location: loc)),
      _value: r.total - r.today,
      firstMonth: date.truncate(t: r._time, unit: 1mo, location: loc),
      firstDay: date.monthDay(t: r._time, location: loc),
    }))
  |> group(columns: ["series"])

energy = union(tables: [firstRow |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value", "series"]), monthEnd])
  |> sort(columns: ["_time"])
  |> difference(nonNegative: true)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._time >= shownFrom)

join(tables: {e: energy, f: firstRow |> keep(columns: ["series", "firstMonth", "firstDay"])}, on: ["series"])
  |> map(fn: (r) => {
      partialStart = r._time == r.firstMonth and r.firstDay > 1
      current = r._time == thisMonth
      label = months[date.month(t: r._time, location: loc) - 1] + " " + string(v: date.year(t: r._time, location: loc))
      startDay = string(v: r.firstDay) + (if r.firstDay >= 11 and r.firstDay <= 13 then "th" else if r.firstDay % 10 == 1 then "st" else if r.firstDay % 10 == 2 then "nd" else if r.firstDay % 10 == 3 then "rd" else "th")
      suffix = if partialStart and current then " (from " + startDay + ", so far)" else if partialStart then " (from " + startDay + ")" else if current then " (so far)" else ""
      return {_time: r._time, _value: r._value, series: r.series, Month: label + suffix}
    })
  |> group()
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["_time", "Month"], columnKey: ["series"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> sort(columns: ["_time"])
  |> keep(columns: ["Month", "Solar", "Consumption"])

panels.title: About these numbers
panels.description: Definitions and data caveats for this dashboard.

options.content:
**Source.** EG4 12000XP counters read from the EG4 cloud. A new sample arrives only when EG4 publishes (about every 1–2 min, sometimes 5 min); check *Data freshness* first.

**Solar** is the combined yield of both MPPT inputs. The cloud has no per-string energy (it is stored as `pv1_energy_*`).

**Consumption** is the inverter's backup (EPS) output, i.e. what the house used.

**History starts 8 May 2026** (install day). Everything before 26 Sep 2026 18:26 was imported from the EG4 portal's data export (~4-min rows); later data is recorded live. Days or months without samples are left out, not drawn as zero. Today and this month are marked *(so far)*; the first month is marked with the day it starts on.

**Self-sufficiency** cannot subtract generator energy because the cloud has no generator-energy counter; *Generator today* flags a day on which the generator was seen running (the percentage is then overstated).
